author: beehive state news
title: Utah State track and field sends 22 athletes to NCAA West First Rounds
text:
Utah State University announced on May 26 that its track and field team will send 22 qualified athletes to compete at the 2026 NCAA West First Rounds, held at John McDonnell Field in Fayetteville, Arkansas, from May 27 to May 30.
The meet features the region’s top competitors, with berths awarded to the top 48 individuals and top 24 relay teams in each event. Utah State’s contingent will participate in a total of 21 events. Director of Track & Field/Cross Country Artie Gulden said, “We are super proud to have 22 student-athletes at the NCAA West First Rounds. Many have been here before, but we have a good number who are here for the first time. This meet is really just about execution. If they can achieve similar marks that got them here, we should be in a good position to have some move on to the NCAA finals.”
Seven Aggies are making their debut appearance at this stage of competition: juniors Kace Jones, Michael Amitava Maiorano and Joshua McKee; freshman David Konan; junior Claire Petersen; sophomore Shay Jones; and freshman Karina Cooper. Several others bring prior experience—senior Logan Hammer is competing for his fourth time after advancing to nationals in previous years, while graduate Logan Garnica and juniors Landon Bott, Walker Deede and Shelby Jensen are each making their third appearance.
Utah State athletes set multiple school records during the season leading up to this meet. Garnica broke his own record in the men’s steeplechase with a time of 8:29.92 at the Bryan Clay Invitational. Sarah Ellis set a new women’s record in the 5,000 meters with a time of 15:50.07. Valerie Clark broke Utah State’s women’s javelin record with a throw of 53.60 meters at home during the Aggie Invitational, while Ayodele Ojo Jr.’s performance at the Mountain West Outdoor Championships established a new school mark for men’s 100 meters.
In addition to individual achievements, Utah State student-athletes earned several conference awards throughout both indoor and outdoor seasons—highlighted by Henry Tait’s Freshman of the Week honor on March 24 and Karina Cooper’s women’s freshman recognition on March 31.
At their most recent outing—the Mountain West Outdoor Track and Field Championships—the men placed third while the women finished eighth overall as four titles were claimed along with multiple medals.
